hypotheses_tested: H1 (the assignment's item 2 — is the change since r6 genuinely comment-only, or did a code token move with it?): REJECTED as a risk, proven two independent ways. (a) `jj diff --from 2e61e36b --to @` touches exactly one file, src/main/document/store.ts, and every added/removed line begins with " * " — I counted the diff's +/- lines that do NOT start with " * " and got 0. (b) Structural proof rather than diff-reading: the leading module docblock is the only region touched (old lines 1-95, new lines 1-94, both terminating at the sole top-level ` */`), so I stripped it from both revisions and ran `cmp` on the remainder — the post-docblock bytes are byte-for-byte identical. Zero code tokens changed; the 184-test result is therefore expected to be, and is, unchanged. (A TypeScript-scanner token diff was my first plan and is not possible here: the repo is on typescript@7.0.2, whose package exposes no CJS `createScanner` API. The byte-identical-body comparison is strictly stronger anyway.)

H2 (the assignment's item 1 — is r6's minor actually fixed, and did the rewrite introduce comment drift?): REJECTED as a defect, with one cosmetic residue recorded as the minor above. The second "So" is gone (line 25 now opens "Extraction is driven by *our own* validated central-directory scan"), and the mid-sentence break r6 quoted ("...regardless of how many members the archive has, and a / member whose stream produces...") is gone — "and a member whose stream produces more bytes than it declared is aborted mid-inflate rather than trusted" is now one continuous sentence. No factual claim in the paragraph was altered: I diffed the prose word-for-word and the only edits are the dropped "So " and the re-wrapping. What the reflow did leave behind is a 121-char line, which is the minor.

H3 (does the reflowed paragraph still state a bound the code actually honours? — the specific check the assignment asked for): REJECTED as drift; the numbers are right and I re-derived them from the constants rather than from r6's write-up. Line 29 claims peak allocation is `largest single allowed member + ~2 MB (see inflateMember)`. In `inflateMember` (store.ts:596) the retained buffer is `new Uint8Array(allowed)` — exactly one member's declared, cap-approved size — and the transient overshoot is bounded by the feed sizing at store.ts:612-613: once the remaining allowance drops below ~1.05 MB the `headroom` term falls under MIN_FEED_BYTES and the feed clamps to 1024 (store.ts:543), so a single push can hand the callback at most MIN_FEED_BYTES * MAX_DEFLATE_RATIO = 1024 * 1032 = 1.057 MB before the `produced + chunk.length > allowed` check at line 601 sees it, and fflate's internal output buffer doubles, so ~2.11 MB. "~2 MB" is correct, and it agrees with the more detailed statement at store.ts:585-589. MAX_DEFLATE_RATIO is 1032 (store.ts:542), not a stale value.

H4 (does "aborted mid-inflate rather than trusted" — the clause the reflow moved across a line boundary — still describe what the code does?): REJECTED. The `Inflate` callback at store.ts:600-607 sets `overflowed = true` and returns *without* writing the offending chunk (so `out` can never be overrun), the push loop breaks at store.ts:616 on the very next iteration test, and store.ts:618-621 throws ZipTooLargeError. The remaining compressed input is never fed. So the abort really is mid-stream, not a post-hoc audit, and the comment matches. The complementary under-delivery case the next sentence of the function docblock describes (`produced !== allowed`, store.ts:623) is still present and still ordered after the overflow throw, so an overflowing member reports 'too-large' rather than the under-delivery message.

H5 (NEW, fresh-eyes, not in r6's twelve — can the `inflateMember` push loop fail to terminate, i.e. can `feed` be 0 and spin forever under the 30 s deadline?): REJECTED. `feed = Math.min(MAX_FEED_BYTES, Math.max(MIN_FEED_BYTES, headroom), source.length - at)` (store.ts:613). The loop condition guarantees `at < source.length`, so the third term is >= 1; `headroom = ceil((allowed - produced + 1) / 1032)` is >= 1 because the callback maintains `produced <= allowed` (it refuses any chunk that would break that), so the second term is >= MIN_FEED_BYTES = 1024. The minimum of {16384, >=1024, >=1} is therefore >= 1 and `at` strictly increases every iteration — no zero-feed spin, and the loop is bounded by `source.length` pushes. The `Date.now() > deadline` check at line 611 is a second, independent bound rather than the only one.

H6 (NEW, fresh-eyes — is the module docblock's "regardless of how many members the archive has" misleading about total process memory, given `extractMembers` retains every member in `out`?): REJECTED as a finding, judged benign after reading both sides. Strictly, the bytes an N-member read retains are the sum of all members, not one member; the sentence is scoped to the inflation working set, which is the quantity the surrounding paragraph is contrasting against fflate's per-member worker buffers ('peak memory is the *sum* of every member's buffers plus one V8 isolate ... each', lines 14-20). The retained sum is unavoidable — it is the deck the caller asked for — and it is bounded separately and explicitly by the `maxTotalBytes` shrinking budget described in the 'Bounded resources' guarantee at lines 52-55 and enforced at store.ts:645/660. Two adjacent, correctly-scoped claims; not worth a finding, and calling it one would be re-litigating a sentence r6 already validated the numeric half of.

H7 (NEW, fresh-eyes — did the r6->r7 edit disturb anything a test or tool depends on, e.g. a line-number-sensitive test, snapshot, or lint suppression?): REJECTED. The docblock lost one net line (95 -> 94), shifting every subsequent line up by one. Nothing depends on it: no test in tests/unit/document/** references store.ts line numbers, the only `oxlint-disable-next-line` in the changeset sits inline at the sequential-yield await and moved with its statement, and both the full test suite and both tsconfig typecheck passes are green from my own run. Confirmed empirically by the 184/184 result rather than by inspection alone.

notes.summary: Confirmation round on a comment-only edit. All three of the round's stated obligations check out: (1) r6's minor is genuinely fixed — the duplicated "So" opener is gone and the mid-sentence line break is closed, with no factual claim altered; (2) the change is provably comment-only — it touches only the leading module docblock, every diff line starts with " * ", and the post-docblock bytes of the file are byte-for-byte identical to the r6 revision, so zero code tokens moved; (3) my own run of pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck and pnpm test is green at 184/184, the stated baseline. On fresh eyes I re-derived the reflowed paragraph's "~2 MB" peak-allocation bound from MIN_FEED_BYTES (1024) and MAX_DEFLATE_RATIO (1032) and it is correct, confirmed the "aborted mid-inflate" clause still matches the overflow path, and proved the push loop cannot spin on a zero-length feed. The one thing left is that the reflow itself was not quite finished: it produced a 121-char line in a docblock that was previously entirely within the repo's 100-column printWidth. Prettier will never flag it. Ship it; fix the wrap whenever the file is next opened.
